title: Severe Trauma, High Falls, and Suspected Fractures
source_citation: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) International First Aid Guidelines 2020; American College of Surgeons (ACS) Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) Principles

steps.text_key: Call 112 immediately for falls from height, vehicular impact, severe deformity, or inability to move limbs
Check for responsiveness and clear breathing without moving the patient's head or spine
Keep the patient completely still: stabilize the head and neck in the position found using your hands on both sides
Control any life-threatening external bleeding with direct pressure, taking care not to push on bone fragments
Support deformed or fractured limbs in the position found using soft padding, rolled blankets, or pillows on either side
Keep the patient warm and calm, monitoring consciousness continuously until paramedics arrive

do_not: Do not move the patient unless there is immediate danger to life (fire, structural collapse, explosion)
Do not attempt to realign, straighten, or force a deformed limb or joint back into place
Do not push exposed bone ends back under the skin in an open fracture
Do not allow the patient to stand up, walk, or sit upright after a high-impact fall
